findings.title: The WD case rule bypasses the exhaustive (i)-(iii) test and has no control
findings.section: Step 3 class table, Implementation defect (line 284); class rules, Retrospective design (lines 296-302); admission rule (line 437)
findings.problem:
Draft 3 follows F1's form of the WD route, which supersedes C7's. The new text brings back the kind of contradiction F2 removed.
(1) Line 284 defines when an alternative counts: only (i) a probe recovery, (ii) prompt omission or contradiction, or (iii) a parameter. WD is none of these. Lines 300-301 still code a case 'implementation choice' when WD carries the value.
(2) Line 298 says a case is coded implementation choice 'if an alternative consistent with the 94c049d text would have prevented it'. It sets no standard of evidence. A page argument then decides, which line 284 forbids ('wording quality without (i)-(iii) does not count').
(3) The per-value test ('WD carries the value in at least 2 of 3 WD runs') has no control. Step 2c already runs three interleaved fresh A1 runs. A value those runs also carry in 2 or 3 of 3 is sampling instability, not a WD effect. That is the k0 logic of the probe rule.
(4) 'Otherwise' includes WD carrying the value in 1 of 3. That result is inconclusive under the probe logic, yet it lets the coder argue architectural.
(5) Line 437 calls a non-admitted contract 'a design alternative not taken'. Read for WD, that contradicts the class rule, which treats WD as an implementation alternative.
findings.proposed_change:
1. In line 284, add test (iv): "for `carried:claims_without_the_value`, WD carries the value in at least 2 of 3 WD runs while the interleaved fresh A1 runs carry it in at most 1 of 3."
2. Replace lines 300-302 with: "The alternative is WD, decided by (iv). If the fresh A1 runs carry the value in 2 or 3 of 3, the case is sampling instability (unclear). If WD carries it in exactly 1 of 3, the result is inconclusive and cannot support an architectural or trade-off code. A coder may argue architectural from the quoted 94c049d text (D4's scalar-concept passage) only where WD carries the value in 0 of 3, fresh A1 carries it in at most 1 of 3, and the burden rule is met."
3. In line 298, change "would have prevented it" to "is shown to prevent it under (i)-(iv)".
4. In line 437, write "An A2 contract not admitted is a design alternative not taken." Then add: "If WD is not admitted, cases coded implementation choice under (iv) stay unrepaired implementation defects."

findings.title: A2-only repair checks have no fixed prediction

findings.problem:
C8's reference fixed a prediction for A2-only checks: fewer losses at the boundary in every gated A2 run, no new incidence, and no row turning pass to lost. Draft 3 lists the check methods: the A2 harness, served support verdicts, and A2' against A2 runs. It states no prediction for any of them.

- The LLM-seam prediction is written for A1' against C.

Also missing is C8's sentence that an A2 repair enters no Step 5 arm while A2 waits for the conflict decision.

Harness and served-support checks: net recovered rows at the boundary, summed over the gate-passing A2 runs where the cause occurs, are above zero and come from at least 3 distinct values; no run has more rows lost at the status step than the recorded A2 replay; there is no new incidence. A2' live runs: the LLM-seam prediction, with the three same-period A2 runs in place of C. An A2-only repair enters no Step 5 arm. It informs only the contracts' development verdicts and their admission."

findings.title: The admission rule does not say whether the recorded or the bounded verdict decides
findings.section: Step 3 bound rule (lines 384-390); Step 4 admission (lines 428-438); Step 2c rule
findings.problem:
F10's reference made the bound rule apply on top of plan 23's verdict rule: 'computed on the recorded outcomes under the verdict rule (P23:269) ... the bounded verdict counts'. Draft 3 separates the two. Line 390 says 'the bounded one counts' for development verdicts. The admission rule (line 436) says only that 'only works is admitted'.
- It is not stated whether WD and each A2 contract are admitted on the recorded or the bounded verdict.
- If the bound applies, it is undefined for the contrasts admission actually uses. The 2c runs and the contract-off states of the leave-one-out have no coded cases. The comparator's 'unrepaired and unclear losses' cannot be counted.
- The two readings can lead to different final configurations. This choice decides outcomes, so it has to be fixed before signing (F0).

In a contrast whose runs are not coded (the 2c runs, and the contract-off states of the leave-one-out), the bound uses the known-bug incidence. For harness contrasts it also uses the gained rows whose pass in the coded recorded A2 run is coded as resting on a defect (or, where unsampled, model pre-coded so), counting them as not gained. No comparator adjustment applies to uncoded runs." If the author prefers the recorded verdict for admission, say so explicitly. In that case the bounded verdict is reported beside it and governs only the development and Phase D statements.

findings.title: Probe (ii): hint-routed claims have no control and map to the wrong sub-cause; (b2) text is not fixed
findings.section: Step 2b (ii) Live (lines 222-224); recovery rule and mapping (lines 227-241); Rules fixed

result.reasoning:
The main claim holds, but the sentence the finding wants to bring back from C8 would now contradict draft 3.

1. **The prediction gap is real.** Lines 420-425 of 23-plan-amendment-1-ceilings-and-root-cause.md list three ways to check an A2-only repair: deterministic logic in the A2 harness, re-run support verdicts served to the harness, and A2' runs against three same-period A2 runs. None of them states a prediction.
   - The state-logic prediction (lines 406-409) is worded for "A1' than under C".
   - The LLM-seam prediction (lines 414-418) is worded for A1' and C runs.
   - So line 426 ("If a prediction fails...") has nothing to apply to an A2-only repair. The acceptance criterion would be set after the result.
   - A reader could map the A2 methods onto those two predictions by analogy, but the draft says so nowhere. Every other check is marked "fixed here", so the gap is real and costs one paragraph to close.

2. **The proposed fix has two defects.**
   - (a) **The "enters no Step 5 arm" sentence is stale.** C8 wrote it against draft 2, where Step 5 ran only A0 and A1/A1'. Draft 3 changed that design:
     - Step 5 (line 447) runs "the final configuration, meaning the reference arm plus each admitted contract";
     - the admission rule (line 435) admits "(b) repairs: a passed Step 4 check";
     - end state 1 (line 22) needs the repair to be "admitted to the final configuration".
     If A2-only repairs could never enter a Step 5 arm, an admitted contract would run in Step 5 without its repair. A2-only losses could then never reach end state 1. Dropping the sentence was consistent with draft 3, so it should not be restored.
   - (b) **The control is unspecified.** The proposed control is "the recorded A2 replay" and "same-period A2 runs". But C is A1 plus the accepted (a) and state-logic repairs, and A2 is A1 plus the four contracts (plan 23 line 130; 23-el2020-arms.md line 62). Comparing A2' with plain A2 would mix the effect of those accepted repairs into the result for the repair under test. The control should be C plus the four contracts.

3. **One more ambiguity.** The draft does not say whether a contract's admission leave-one-out is computed with its A2-only repair on. That choice should also be fixed before any results.

I read draft 3 cold and checked it against the frozen trace, plan 23, the cost facts and the app code. All five frozen-input hashes match. Each A1/A2 run has 59–64 lost cases, so 30 per run is about half. The 2c threshold of 9 rows and 5 values is correct at `carried`. The Step 3 hours add up, Phase C's $32 to date is right (18.34 + 13.67), and the named code entities and parameter values exist as stated (config.py:71-86, cycle2_flags.py, informed_reviewer.py:78, embeddings.py:185).

**Most serious problem (blocking).** The draft does not say whether admission to the final configuration uses the recorded verdict or the bounded one. The bound rule says "the bounded one counts". But it cannot be computed for the runs admission uses:
- the WD and fresh A1 runs;
- the A2 leave-one-out variants.

None of these has a coded sample.

**Five major problems:**
1. **Cost total and budget sentence.** The total line does not follow from the table rows. The stated upper end ($70 without LLM-seam repairs) leaves out three of the table's own items: the read-path screen, the A2-only check and the final-configuration arm. "With one" adds $20 at the bottom and $30 at the top. Phase C crosses plan 23's $100 ceiling on the ordinary path, not only in the tails.
2. **Conformance repairs.** (a) repairs are never "admitted", so their losses can never reach end state 1. Step 5's reference arm ("A1, or A1′") drops them.
3. **WD.** WD has two acceptance routes with different thresholds: the Step 2c rule, and the Step 4(b) check through the implementation-choice class rule. It also carries two labels (implementation alternative and design alternative not taken). Its ES2009 branch contradicts the rule for a missing WD result.
4. **Probe (ii).** Probe (ii) cannot run as written:
   - no pass criterion for a single re-resolution scored against a row-level boundary;
   - no control for hint-routed claims, which make up about two thirds of routing losses;
   - the mapping gives hint-routed claims a resolver sub-cause, which contradicts the within-routing path rule.
5. **Pass 1 and the anchoring measure.** With probe results sealed, the burden rule forces pass 1 to code implementation or unclear wherever the boundary has a probe-type alternative. So the blind kappa and the pass-1/pass-2 "anchoring" rate become largely mechanical.

**Minor problems:**
- Order-of-work errors: V4's blind set refers to pass 2, the model's prompt is fixed before the pilot adds sub-causes, and the codebook revision has no blind trigger.
- Gaps in the probe mapping and an overlap in the recovery table.
- Probe (d) is costed at one repeat.

- A2 admission with fewer than three gate-passing runs.
- The V4 fallback leaves the stopping rule unreachable.
- When the claims register's mapping is finalised is unclear.

- The principle that "every loss" ends in a state, against sample coding.

findings.title: WD has two acceptance routes with different thresholds, two incompatible labels, and an ES2009 branch that contradicts the 'no WD result' rule
findings.section: Step 2c rule (lines 249-257), Retrospective design rule (lines 300-302), candidate causes (line 330), Step 4(b) (lines 398-402, 426), Admission (lines 429, 437), Order of work item 8 (line 359)
findings.problem:
**(1) Two routes.**
- The class rule codes a `carried:claims_without_the_value` case as implementation choice wherever WD carries the value in at least 2 of 3 WD runs. This happens even when WD fails the 2c rule.
- If those cases share a sub-cause (the pilot may add one, since none of the four listed extraction causes fits), they become eligible under Step 4(b) as soon as 3 agreed values exist.
- Ordering is 'by distinct values', and `carried:claims_without_the_value` is the largest extraction sub-code (26–28 rows per run), so it would take the extraction slot.
- 'Not approved' is barred except for infeasibility or cost.
- WD would then be re-tested as an LLM-seam repair under a weaker prediction: at least 5 net rows from 3 values, with ties allowed. The 2c rule requires all runs separated and a mean margin above 9 rows and 5 values.
- So WD can fail the 2c admission rule and still be admitted as a '(b) repair'. Line 426 ('no second attempt') does not clearly forbid this.

**(2) Two labels.** Admission calls a contract that is not admitted 'a design alternative not taken'. The class rule treats WD as 'an alternative consistent with the 94c049d text', i.e. implementation choice.

**(3) ES2009.** For 3b, WD is never run on ES2009, so 'where WD carries the value in at least 2 of 3 WD runs' cannot hold. The 'otherwise' branch then lets a coder argue architectural weakness. Line 257 says that when the WD evidence is missing, the cases are unclear, never architectural.

**(4) Pass 2.** Item 8 lists only the oracle caused-at and the probe mapping as mechanical replacements at pass 2. The WD outcome is not listed (nor the A2 leave-one-out caused-at), although both are fixed rules that need revealed results.
findings.proposed_change:
Add to the WD class rule:

"These cases get the sub-cause 'no whole-decision contract'. Its only remedy is WD, decided solely by the Step 2c rule. It is never eligible under Step 4(b). Its cases are Repaired if WD is admitted. Otherwise they are unrepaired implementation choice where WD carried the value in at least 2 of 3 runs, and unclear where no WD run covers the value (including every ES2009 case unless WD is in the final candidate)."

In Admission, change "A contract not admitted is a design alternative not taken" to apply to the A2 contracts only.

In item 8, add "the WD outcome and the A2 leave-one-out caused-at" to the mechanical replacements.

findings.title: Probe (ii) cannot be scored as written: no pass criterion, no control for hint-routed claims, and a mapping that contradicts the path rule
findings.section: Step 2b preamble (line 212), (ii) Live (line 224), Recovery rule (lines 227-234), Mapping (line 237); Step 3 'Within routing' (line 321)
findings.problem:
**(1) No pass criterion.** k counts repeats 'whose output passes the case's boundary'. A routing-lost case is lost at `proposed:another_value_won` or `current:overwritten_by_non_gold_value`, which are row outcomes of the state rules over every claim on the key. One resolver call re-files one claim. No rule says when a single re-resolution 'passes' proposed or current. Several carriers and rivals are re-resolved per case, each three times, and no rule says how their repeats combine into k. This also contradicts 'Each probe is a single LLM call' (line 212).

**(2) No control for hint-routed claims.** The control exists only 'for resolver-routed claims'. Hint-routed claims have no recorded resolver prompt, so k0 is undefined. Every row of the recovery table needs k0 (≤1 or ≥2), so these cases cannot be classified. They are the majority: 134 of 203 routing-lost rows had every carrier keyed by the hint (line 40).

**(3) Wrong sub-cause.** The mapping turns 'unpruned resolution recovered' into implementation choice with the sub-cause 'a shortlist or prune that excluded the key'. For a hint-routed claim, no shortlist or prune was ever applied. Line 321 says a hint path means key assignment at extraction. The mechanical mapping and the path rule therefore give different boundaries for the same case.
findings.proposed_change:
In (ii) Live, add:

"A repeat passes when each re-resolved carrier is filed under a key whose definition fits the gold value's matter, and each re-resolved rival under a different key. Repeat j of every claim forms output j of the case. Hint-routed claims have no control. Their (ii) result is reported as 'no control' and counts as no probe evidence (at most inconclusive)."

In the Mapping, restrict the unpruned-resolution row to resolver- and expansion-routed claims.

Change line 212 to "one LLM call per claim and repeat".

findings.title: With probe results sealed, the burden rule forces pass 1 at three boundaries, so the blind kappa and the 'anchoring measure' become largely mechanical
findings.section: Class rules: Burden (lines 292-295); Order of work items 4, 7, 8 (lines 349-361); Agreement (lines 363-368); cost table V4 load (line 493)
findings.problem:
A probe-type alternative is 'ruled out only by its probe returning *not recovered*'. Without that, the code must be implementation defect or unclear. Probe outputs are sealed until item 7.

At pass 1, and for the model pre-coder and V4's blind codes, no probe-type alternative can therefore be ruled out. This applies to every case caused at a boundary with such a candidate:
- extraction (registry cut, neutral examples);
- key resolution (shortlist or prune);
- reading (question-time shortlist).

On the frozen trace these are roughly half or more of each A1/A2 run's cases. Three consequences:
- (a) Blind agreement on implementation versus not, for those cases, records the rule rather than the coders' judgement, so the 0.60 target is partly met by construction.
- (b) The pass-1/pass-2 change rate, 'the anchoring measure', will consist mostly of mechanical changes at the reveal: oracle caused-at moves, the probe mapping, and releases where every probe returned not recovered. These are not anchoring. Item 8 logs them but does not separate them.
- (c) V4 must code 'every case that pass 1 or the model classes as implementation'. If coders use implementation rather than unclear here, the forced cases enter that set, and 'about 100–140 cases' is likely low.
findings.proposed_change:
At pass 1 and in V4's blind codes, let a case whose only open alternative is probe-type be coded "pending probe", with the coder's conditional class if the probe returns not recovered. Compute blind kappa on the conditional classes.

Report the anchoring measure over changes that are not mechanical only. Mechanical changes (oracle, probe mapping, WD outcome, leave-one-out) are logged and counted apart.

Re-estimate V4's load after this rule.

findings.title: The probe mapping has unmapped combinations and an impossible condition, and the recovery table overlaps
findings.section: Step 2b Recovery rule and Mapping (lines 227-241)

**Overlap in the recovery table.** k = 1 with k0 ≥ 2 is both 'Inconclusive' and 'Not reproduced'. Only 'Not reproduced' carries the sub-cause 'sampling instability'.

findings.title: Probe (d) is costed at one repeat, but runs three
findings.section: Step 2b (line 219) and cost table row 2b (line 491)
findings.problem:
The recovery rule gives every condition three repeats, so (d) has three. '(d) about $4' is the round-2 figure for one gpt-5.4 call on each of about 152 cases (about 8k input tokens per recorded extraction prompt, about $0.025 a call).

findings.title: Misstated figures in 'Already read', and harm margins set below the noise the draft itself uses
findings.section: Already read (lines 35, 43, 44), Step 2b (line 216), Step 2c (lines 251-252), Step 4 LLM-seam prediction (lines 416-418)
findings.problem:
**Line 35.** 'The largest within-arm range at a boundary is 9 rows and 5 distinct values' holds only at `carried` (current rows: A0 25/33/31, A1 28/24/33). At other steps the ranges are larger: `current` in A0 is 18/29/25 (11 rows, 6 values). At the grouped boundaries of the results file they are larger still: extraction in A0 39/52/47 and filing in A1 21/34/22 (13 rows each).

result.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. All three parts hold against draft 3 as written.

1. **An (a) repair can never be coded "Repaired".**
   - Line 22 requires that the repair "passed its check *and* was admitted to the final configuration".
   - (a) repairs are "accepted" (line 396) and placed in C (line 405), which is only the Step 4 control configuration.
   - The admission subsection (lines 428-438) lists only WD, each A2 contract and (b) repairs, and then says "Only *works* is admitted". (a) repairs appear nowhere in it.
   - One could defend the draft by pointing to plan 23, which defines A1 as "bugs fixed" (plan 23 line 129 and D3 line 337). On that reading a conformance fix would fall into A1 automatically. But the amendment's own line 405 says "C is A1 plus every accepted (a) repair", so within this file A1 explicitly excludes (a) repairs. The two readings conflict, and a rules document signed before outcomes should not leave the reader to choose between them.

2. **Step 5's reference arm drops the (a) repairs.**
   - Line 446 says "A1, or A1′ if Step 4 admits a repair".
   - With (a) repairs but no admitted (b) repair, the reference arm is A1 without the conformance fixes. The (a) repairs then reach the final configuration only if some unrelated (b) repair happens to be admitted.
   - The draft makes this scenario likely, not a corner case. Under the V4 fallback (line 370), Step 4(b) is skipped and "only (a) conformance repairs proceed".
   - Line 446 also carries this reference into Phase D3, so the gap would propagate to the registration.

3. **A1′ is undefined when more than one repair is admitted.**
   - Line 405 defines A1′ per repair: "C plus the repair under test".
   - Step 4 allows one repair per boundary plus an A2-only slot (line 400), so several A1′ configurations can each pass their own check.
   - C already accumulates accepted state-logic repairs. LLM-seam and read-path repairs, however, are each checked against C alone.
   - Step 5 and Phase D3 therefore name a configuration that does not exist once two or more repairs are admitted.

**Not handled elsewhere.** Round-2 findings F0 and C7 introduced the admission rule and the A1′ reference arm. Neither addressed (a) repairs or several admitted repairs.

**Not cosmetic.** The reference arm is the no-contract comparator for every contract verdict, both in Step 5 and in the registration.

**Where the proposed fix needs changes.**
- Naming the reference configuration "R" clashes with the routing oracle R, which lines 183-194 and 315-320 use throughout, and with plan 23's "batch R".
- Putting A2-only (b) repairs into the no-contract reference is conceptually wrong. They belong with their contract.
- Line 271 still says "the final candidate", a term the draft no longer defines.
- Line 438 ("A (b) repair that passes its check but is not admitted") cannot happen once line 435 makes a passed check the admission criterion. It should be reworded while this subsection is being edited.

A1-ref replaces A1 as the no-contract reference for every contract verdict, here and in Phase D3. An admitted A2-only repair enters only together with its contract, in the final configuration."

4. **Step 5, disclosure (add under Framing):**

result.reasoning:
I checked the finding against draft 3, plan 23 line 269 and round-2 findings F0 and F10. It holds. It also misses one point, and its proposed fix would make that point active.

**1. Which verdict admits is only implied, not stated.**
- The chain does exist. P23:269 says admission uses "the rule the registration will use (Phase D3)". The bound rule (line 390) says "the bounded one counts" and calls itself "the dry run of the rule that the registration will carry into Phase D3". F10's adopted text tied the bound to the P23:269 verdict, so the bounded reading is what was meant.
- But the Admission section (428-438) never names the bound. The 2c rule reads as self-contained ("WD *works* ... only if all of these hold"). And "dry run" gives someone a textual reason to say the bound is a rehearsal that does not govern admission. Because the amendment exists to remove choices that could be made after the outcomes are seen, that ambiguity is enough to justify an edit.

**2. The bound cannot be computed for the runs admission uses.**
- The 3a sample is 6 × 30 = 180 cases from the frozen six A1/A2 runs (line 268). The pages are built from the frozen trace right after signing (line 346). So none of these is coded:
  - the 2c WD runs and the fresh A1 runs;
  - the C and A1′ runs from the LLM-seam checks;
  - the A2 leave-one-out variants.
- The bound needs a sample share and a share of defect-resting passes for each run. Nothing says where those come from for an uncoded run.

**3. The A0 clause is a leftover.** "For unsampled A0 cases, the model pre-code is used where it is higher" has nothing to compare against. Line 269 now gives A0 no author sample, and A0 feeds no admission verdict.

**What the finding misses.** In an on/off contrast, the bound counts the comparator's unrepaired implementation losses as recovered (line 386). Take WD:
- The class rule (lines 300-302) codes A1's `carried:claims_without_the_value` cases as *implementation choice* exactly where WD carries the value.
- Before admission those cases are unrepaired. So the bound counts the comparator's losses that WD recovers as already recovered, and WD's measured effect disappears.
- The same happens to a (b) repair, judged against C's cases coded with the cause it repairs. It also happens to an A2 contract, judged against the losses its leave-one-out recovers.

Every contract and repair would then come out *can't tell* by construction. Taking the comparator's shares from "the same arm's 3a sample", as the finding proposes, makes this circularity active. The A1 share at `carried` is also a poor stand-in for WD runs' own losses, because its implementation codes mean "WD would fix this".

So the finding stands, but its fix needs this exclusion added.
